concepts.name: Hangul consonant letters
concepts.summary: Recognise and pronounce the basic consonant letters and know how their shapes relate to place of articulation.

concepts.name: Hangul vowel letters
concepts.summary: Recognise and pronounce basic vowels, including vertical and horizontal vowel shapes and the contrast of ㅓ/ㅗ and ㅡ/ㅜ.

concepts.name: Syllable block construction
concepts.summary: Explain how consonants and vowels combine into square syllable blocks and read blocks left-to-right and top-to-bottom.

concepts.name: Batchim final consonants
concepts.summary: Understand that a consonant at the bottom of a block is pronounced as one of seven representative sounds.

concepts.name: Aspirated and tense consonants
concepts.summary: Distinguish plain, aspirated and tense consonant triplets such as ㄱ/ㅋ/ㄲ in sound and spelling.

concepts.name: Basic greetings and polite phrases
concepts.summary: Remember common expressions like 안녕하세요, 감사합니다 and 네/아니요 and when they are used.

concepts.name: SOV word order
concepts.summary: Understand that Korean sentences place the verb at the end, with other elements before it.

misconceptions.text: Hangul letters are written in a line like the Latin alphabet rather than grouped into blocks.
Every batchim consonant is pronounced exactly as its letter name suggests.
ㅇ at the start of a block is pronounced like the 'ng' sound.

concepts.name: Topic and subject particles
concepts.summary: Choose 은/는 and 이/가 by final-sound form and apply them to mark topic versus subject.

concepts.name: Object and location particles
concepts.summary: Use 을/를 for objects and 에 and 에서 for destinations, existence locations and action locations.

concepts.name: Present-tense 해요 style
concepts.summary: Conjugate verbs and adjectives into the polite 해요 form including 하다 verbs and vowel harmony.

concepts.name: Formal 합니다 style
concepts.summary: Form the formal polite ending by checking whether the stem ends in a vowel or consonant.

concepts.name: Native Korean numbers
concepts.summary: Count and state age and hours with native numbers and their counter-form changes.

concepts.name: Sino-Korean numbers
concepts.summary: Use Sino-Korean numbers for dates, money, minutes and phone numbers, and pick the right set by context.

concepts.name: Copula 이다 and 있다/없다
concepts.summary: Express identity with 이에요/예요 and existence or possession with 있어요/없어요.

concepts.name: Liaison and nasalisation sound changes
concepts.summary: Apply linking of batchim to a following vowel and nasalisation to predict actual pronunciation.

misconceptions.text: 은/는 and 이/가 are interchangeable and both simply mean 'is'.
Native and Sino-Korean numbers can be used freely in any context.
Korean needs an explicit subject in every sentence.

concepts.name: Irregular verb conjugation
concepts.summary: Conjugate ㅂ, ㄷ, ㅅ, ㅡ, 르 and ㅎ irregular stems correctly before vowel endings.

concepts.name: Past and future tense endings
concepts.summary: Form past with -았/었- and future or conjecture with -(으)ㄹ 거예요 and use them appropriately.

concepts.name: Subject honorific -(으)시-
concepts.summary: Add -(으)시- to the verb and swap honorific vocabulary such as 드시다 and 계시다 for respected subjects.

concepts.name: Connective endings
concepts.summary: Distinguish sequence, cause and contrast connectives and choose the ending that fits the logical relation.

concepts.name: Counters and quantity expressions
concepts.summary: Combine numbers with counters like 명, 개, 권 and 시 using the correct number set.

concepts.name: Negation patterns
concepts.summary: Differentiate 안 (will not) from 못 (cannot) and short from long negation.

concepts.name: Tensification and aspiration rules
concepts.summary: Analyse when stops are tensed or ㅎ merges with neighbours to produce aspiration and predict pronunciation.

concepts.name: Modifier forms of verbs
concepts.summary: Build noun-modifying clauses with tense-sensitive endings and distinguish verb from adjective forms.

misconceptions.text: Irregular verbs follow no pattern and must be memorised one by one.
-아서/어서 and -(으)니까 are fully interchangeable for giving reasons.
안 and 못 both simply mean 'not' with no difference in meaning.

concepts.name: Speech level selection
concepts.summary: Judge which of the speech levels, from 합쇼체 to 반말, suits relationship, setting and intent.

concepts.name: Object honorifics and humble forms
concepts.summary: Analyse humble verbs such as 드리다 and 뵙다 and decide when lowering oneself is appropriate versus raising the subject.

concepts.name: Nuance of sentence-final endings
concepts.summary: Differentiate endings expressing confirmation, surprise, discovery and softening and select by speaker stance.

concepts.name: Reported speech
concepts.summary: Convert direct statements, questions, commands and suggestions into indirect quotations with correct endings.

concepts.name: Passive and causative constructions
concepts.summary: Analyse how suffixes and periphrastic forms create passive and causative meanings and when each is natural.

concepts.name: Auxiliary verb constructions
concepts.summary: Interpret aspect and attempt meanings from auxiliary verbs attached to main verbs.

concepts.name: Sino-Korean and native vocabulary
concepts.summary: Use Sino-Korean word roots to infer meaning and judge when native or Sino-Korean synonyms fit better.

concepts.name: Evaluating natural phrasing
concepts.summary: Critique learner sentences for unnatural particle, subject and politeness choices and justify corrections.

misconceptions.text: Dropping to 반말 is fine with anyone once you have met a few times.
Honorific -시- can be used for oneself to be polite.
Passive suffixes work like English passives and can be applied to any transitive verb.

concepts.name: Pragmatic register shifting
concepts.summary: Evaluate and manage shifts between registers to signal distance, intimacy, authority or irony.

concepts.name: Discourse topic and information structure
concepts.summary: Evaluate how 은/는, 이/가, ellipsis and word scrambling organise given and new information.

concepts.name: Written and spoken style variation
concepts.summary: Judge differences among news, academic, literary and conversational Korean, including the 한다체.

concepts.name: Idiomatic and sino-compound expression
concepts.summary: Evaluate and apply idioms, proverbs and four-character compounds with appropriate nuance.

concepts.name: Dialect and sociolinguistic variation
concepts.summary: Assess how dialects, generational slang and North-South differences affect comprehension and usage.

concepts.name: Composing culturally apt texts
concepts.summary: Create emails, essays and speeches in Korean with register, vocabulary and rhetoric suited to audience.

concepts.name: Translation between Korean and English
concepts.summary: Produce translations that handle dropped subjects, honorific information and word-order differences faithfully.

misconceptions.text: Standard Seoul Korean is the only form that matters, and dialects are just mistakes.
Translating means preserving every particle and honorific literally.
The 한다체 plain style is rude and never appropriate in writing.
